```{r}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

config <- yaml::read_yaml(here("r/abrolhos/05_lobster/00_config.yml"))
name <- config$name
legal_size_mm <- config$legal_size_mm
large_male_mm <- config$large_male_mm

tidy_dir   <- here("data/abrolhos/tidy/lobster")
plot_dir   <- here("plots/abrolhos/lobster")
output_dir <- here("output/model-output/abrolhos/lobster")

pots <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-pots_all-years.csv")),
                 colClasses = c(pot_number = "character"))
measurements <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-measurements_all-years.csv")),
                         colClasses = c(pot_number = "character"))
catch_per_pot <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-per-pot.csv")),
                          colClasses = c(pot_number = "character"))
catch_by_zone <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-by-zone.csv")))

# Figures quoted in the modelling text, derived rather than typed in so they
# cannot drift away from the data
n_strings <- dplyr::n_distinct(catch_per_pot$string)

# A string counts as inside or outside only if all of its pots fall in one zone.
# String 14 crosses the boundary and is deliberately left whole, so it is in
# neither count.
strings_by_zone <- catch_per_pot %>%
  group_by(string) %>%
  summarise(zones = n_distinct(zone), zone = first(zone), .groups = "drop")

n_npz_strings <- sum(strings_by_zone$zones == 1 &
                       strings_by_zone$zone %in% "National Park Zone")
n_spz_strings <- sum(strings_by_zone$zones == 1 &
                       !strings_by_zone$zone %in% "National Park Zone")

# Pots reaching the models, after the 0 m depth pot and any missing depth drop
n_pots_model <- sum(!is.na(catch_per_pot$depth_m) & catch_per_pot$depth_m > 0)

pct_zero_large <- round(100 * mean(catch_per_pot$n_male_large == 0))
```

## Survey effort

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of western rock lobster pot sampling on Yamatji Shallow Bank in the 2025 and 2026 surveys, showing the number of pots deployed, the number of pots that fished successfully and were counted, and the number of lobsters measured in each management zone. NPZ = National Park Zone (no take), SPZ = Special Purpose Zone (open to commercial and recreational fishing). Pots that were lost, had a missing trap door, or were flagged in the field as not countable are deployed but not counted."
pots %>%
  group_by(Year = year, Zone = zone) %>%
  summarise(`Pots deployed` = n(),
            `Pots counted` = sum(successful), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(
    measurements %>%
      filter(species %in% "Western Rock Lobster") %>%
      count(Year = year, Zone = zone, name = "Lobsters measured"),
    by = c("Year", "Zone")
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Locations of lobster pots on Yamatji Shallow Bank, shown separately for the 2025 and 2026 surveys. Commonwealth marine park zone boundaries and 10 m depth contours are shown. ABMP = Abrolhos Marine Park (Commonwealth)."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-pot-locations_year.png")))
```

## Abundance

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Western rock lobster catch rates by zone and survey year, showing the number of pots counted, the total number of lobsters caught, and the mean and standard error of the number of lobsters per pot for all lobsters and for legal sized lobsters. Pots that caught no lobsters are included as zeros. Catch is reported per pot rather than per pot-hour because set times were not recorded in 2026."
catch_by_zone %>%
  transmute(Year = year, Zone = zone, `Pots` = n_pots,
            `Total lobsters` = total_lobsters,
            `Mean per pot` = round(mean_per_pot, 2),
            `SE` = round(se_per_pot, 2),
            `Mean legal per pot` = round(mean_legal, 2),
            `SE legal` = round(se_legal, 2)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-rate_zone-year.png")))
```

## Size structure

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of western rock lobster carapace length by zone and survey year, showing the number of lobsters measured, the mean, median, minimum and maximum carapace length, and the percentage of measured lobsters above the legal minimum size. The minimum legal carapace length for western rock lobster is 76 mm."
measurements %>%
  filter(species %in% "Western Rock Lobster", !is.na(carapace_length_mm)) %>%
  group_by(Year = year, Zone = zone) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Mean length (mm)` = round(mean(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `Median (mm)` = round(median(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `Min` = round(min(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `Max` = round(max(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `% legal` = round(100 * mean(carapace_length_mm > legal_size_mm), 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable()
```

## Modelling: catch inside vs outside the National Park Zone

Catch per pot was modelled with a negative binomial generalised linear mixed
model (log link), fitted in `glmmTMB`:

`catch ~ status * year + depth_z + (1 | string)`

where `status` is inside or outside the National Park Zone, `year` is a factor,
`depth_z` is pot depth standardised to zero mean and unit variance, and `string`
is the line of pots that each pot belonged to. Predicted means and standard
errors for each status-by-year combination were obtained with `emmeans`, holding
depth at its mean.

Pots were set in strings of roughly 8 to 20 pots, and the same
`r n_strings` strings were fished in both survey years. Individual pots were not
dropped in exactly the same positions each year, so the `(1 | string)` term acts
as the spatial pairing that makes the between-year comparison like for like. It
is not a claim that a string is a biologically coherent unit: a long string spans
several kilometres, so its two ends are not interchangeable. Because year is
compared within strings its standard error is reduced, while status is compared
almost entirely between strings and its standard error is roughly doubled
relative to a model fitted without the term.

The specification was originally a Tweedie model. Tweedie could not be fitted to
the two sparsest responses once the random effect was included: legal males and
large males both terminated with a non-positive-definite Hessian and no usable
standard errors, and the large male string variance diverged, giving predictions
several times the observed means. The Tweedie power parameter is weakly
identified against the random effect variance when the response is mostly zeros,
which is the case for large males (`r pct_zero_large`% of counted pots caught
none). The negative binomial has no such parameter, fits all six responses
cleanly, and is the conventional choice for integer counts.

Six responses were modelled with this specification: legal catch, sublegal catch,
legal males, legal females, males of `r large_male_mm` mm or more, and all
lobsters combined. These are not independent tests of each other. Legal male and
legal female catch together make up the legal catch, apart from
`r sum(measurements$sex %in% "Unknown" & measurements$size_class %in% "Legal")`
legal animals whose sex was not recorded; the large males are a subset of the
legal males (`r sum(measurements$sex %in% "Male" & measurements$carapace_length_mm >= large_male_mm)`
of `r sum(measurements$sex %in% "Male" & measurements$size_class %in% "Legal")`);
and the all lobsters response is the legal and sublegal responses added together.

::: {.callout-important}
## Two limitations to read these results against

**Status is spatially confounded with survey area.** The National Park Zone is a
single contiguous block that was fished on its own day in both years. Comparing
inside with outside is therefore partly comparing the middle area with the
northern and southern areas, and any habitat difference between those areas is
not separable from the effect of protection.

**Replication for the status comparison is the number of strings, not the number
of pots.** Of the `r n_strings` strings, `r n_npz_strings` sit entirely inside
the National Park Zone and `r n_spz_strings` entirely outside it; only one string
crosses the boundary, so almost all of the status contrast is between strings
rather than within them. The effective sample size for status is therefore closer
to `r n_strings` than to the `r n_pots_model` pots counted, and the standard
errors on the status terms below reflect that. The between-year comparison is not
affected in the same way, because it is made within strings.
:::

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted western rock lobster catch per pot from the negative binomial generalised linear mixed model, by size class, zoning status and survey year, with standard errors and asymptotic 95% confidence limits. Predictions are made with depth held at its mean. NPZ = National Park Zone."
read.csv(file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-predictions.csv"))) %>%
  transmute(`Size class` = size_class, Status = status, Year = year,
            `Per pot` = round(mean, 2),
            SE = round(se, 2),
            `Lower CL` = round(asymp.LCL, 2),
            `Upper CL` = round(asymp.UCL, 2)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Predicted western rock lobster catch per pot inside and outside the National Park Zone across the size progression from sublegal to legal to large males, from the negative binomial generalised linear mixed model. Points are predicted means with standard errors, with depth held at its mean. Note that each panel has its own y axis scale. Legal size is a carapace length greater than 76 mm. NPZ = National Park Zone."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-control-plot_size-progression.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Predicted western rock lobster catch per pot inside and outside the National Park Zone for all five size class models, including legal males and legal females separately, from the negative binomial generalised linear mixed model. Points are predicted means with standard errors, with depth held at its mean. Note that each panel has its own y axis scale. NPZ = National Park Zone."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-control-plot.png")))
```

```{r}

Points are predicted means with standard errors, with depth held at its mean. This response is the sum of the legal and sublegal responses shown above rather than an independent size class. NPZ = National Park Zone."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-control-plot_total.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Predicted western rock lobster catch per pot inside and outside the National Park Zone by size class and survey year, from the negative binomial generalised linear mixed model, shown as bars with standard errors. Depth is held at its mean and each panel has its own y axis scale. NPZ = National Park Zone."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-barplot.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Observed western rock lobster catch per pot by size class, zoning status and survey year, showing the spread of the raw counts behind the modelled means. Boxes show the median and interquartile range with whiskers to 1.5 times the interquartile range. All panels share a y axis so that size classes can be compared against each other. Pots that caught no lobsters are included as zeros. NPZ = National Park Zone."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-boxplot.png")))
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Coefficients of the negative binomial generalised linear mixed model of western rock lobster catch per pot, on the log scale, with standard errors, z statistics and p values. Reference levels are outside the National Park Zone in 2025, so the status term is the effect of protection in 2025 and the interaction term is the change in that effect by 2026. NPZ = National Park Zone."
read.csv(file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-coefficients.csv"))) %>%
  transmute(`Size class` = size_class, Term = term,
            Estimate = round(estimate, 3),
            SE = round(se, 3),
            z = round(z, 2),
            p = if_else(p < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Likelihood ratio test of the status by year interaction for each size class, comparing the full model with an additive model in which the difference between zones is held constant across years. A significant result would indicate that the difference between zones changed between 2025 and 2026."
read.csv(file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-interaction-tests.csv"))) %>%
  transmute(`Size class` = size_class,
            `Chi squared` = round(chisq, 3), df = df,
            p = round(p, 3)) %>%
  kable()
```

## Data notes

- Pots that were lost, had a missing trap door, or were flagged in the field as
  not countable are excluded from catch rates but retained in the pot table.
- Neither survey export records a string identifier, and the 2026 pot numbering
  does not follow position along the line, so strings were assigned by hand from
  the deployment order and pot positions. A string is one physical line of pots
  and is kept whole: one string crosses the National Park Zone boundary and has
  not been split, so that it still represents a single deployment.
- Pots that caught no lobsters are carried through the analysis as zeros.
- Set times were not recorded in 2026, so soak time is available for 2025 only
  and catch is reported per pot rather than per pot-hour.
- 2026 includes six extra pots labelled `F3`, `F3-2` and `FIII`. These are kept
  as distinct pots rather than merged with the numbered pots.
- Three 2026 pots lost GPS fix on retrieval; corrected positions were read from
  the field comments.
- One 2026 pot was logged at 0 m depth, which is not a possible seabed depth
  here. It is treated as missing and drops from the models.
- Non-lobster catch from 2026 is written to a separate bycatch file and is not
  included in these results.
- One 2025 measurement of 24 mm (National Park Zone, pot 2) sits well below the
  next smallest lobster at 50 mm and is likely a data entry error. It has been
  retained pending confirmation.
